subject: Evaluation kickoff & trial plan – Acme Corp
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Li <daniel.li@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation kickoff & trial plan – Acme Corp

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through Acme's use case. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can get the evaluation kicked off: 

- Goal: Validate whether Redwood can reduce inference cost by ~30% while meeting 95th-pct latency SLO for Acme's customer-facing summarization flow.
- Success criteria (proposed):
  - End-to-end latency (95th): <= 350ms for 1k token context in our staging environment
  - Precision on core summarization prompt set: >= 0.88 F1 (as measured by your eval set)
  - Cost per 1k tokens: target <= $0.015 after batching/quantization tuning

Next steps: schedule an evaluation kickoff (trial plan + roles + data/prompts). Neha (SE) will lead the technical kickoff and setup; Marissa will own success criteria and evaluation logistics.

Proposed 60–75min slots this week:
- Thu 11/19 10:00–11:15 PT
- Thu 11/19 14:00–15:15 PT
- Fri 11/20 09:30–10:45 PT

I've attached a draft eval plan and prompt set template (ACME-Redwood-Eval-Plan-v1.pdf, acme-prompt-set.csv). Please pick a slot that works or share alternatives. Also confirm who from your side should join the kickoff (engineering + security recommended).

If useful, I can include a short technical demo at the top (10–15min) and then hand off to Neha for environment/trial setup.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Connor —

Thanks for the concise recap, that aligns with what we discussed. We'd like to move forward with a kickoff next week. Tentatively Sara (Product) and I will join; I'll ask our lead engineer (Victor) to attend the technical portion.

Of the slots you proposed, Thu 11/19 14:00–15:15 PT works best for us. If Neha needs a slightly longer window for walkthrough + initial setup, we can extend to 90 minutes.

A couple of quick asks before the call:
- Can you share an agenda with timings?
- We'll need to know whether the trial will require any inbound firewall rules (we prefer to test via a staging VPC or a limited IP allowlist).
- For the prompt set, we've got a few proprietary examples we can't share in raw form — is it OK to provide redacted examples or metrics instead?

Thanks,
Daniel

Thanks Daniel — happy to take the technical lead on the kickoff. Confirming Thu 11/19 14:00–15:30 PT (I'll plan for a 90-minute session). Proposed rough agenda below:

1) 0–10m: Quick intros + 10–15m demo of Redwood inference pipeline (Connor)
2) 15–35m: Trial architecture & requirements (Neha) — VPC vs hosted staging, auth, IP allowlist, data handling
3) 35–65m: Prompt set + eval metrics alignment (Marissa + Daniel) — review redacted examples and mapping to success criteria
4) 65–90m: Next steps: access, test data ingest, timelines, ownership

Prep items for Acme:
- Please upload a redacted sample of 50 prompts (CSV) to the shared drive or paste examples in the thread — redactions are fine
- Add Victor (eng lead) to the calendar invite so we can go over network/auth
- Confirm whether you'll want SSO/SAML configured for the trial (we can demo scoped API keys otherwise)

I've attached a prompt-set template that shows the columns we'd like (id, prompt, expected_summary, notes). If you prefer, we can accept a metrics-only CSV and map to your redacted prompts during the call.

Looking forward to it — I've reserved the slot on my calendar for now.
